# core/tls13hs.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/tls13hs.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The first two messages of a TLS 1.3 handshake (RFC
8446 section 4): the ClientHello a client sends and the reading of the
ServerHello that answers it, for the cipher suite
TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 and the key exchange X25519.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, a ClientHello
has the length its fields add up to, and `tls13_parse_server_hello` reads
no byte outside the message it is given, whatever it holds. Not proved:
that a ClientHello is one a server accepts (the tests compare it with one
assembled by another program) or that the reader accepts every ServerHello
of the standard (it takes the one suite and group the client offered).

`import "core/tls13hs.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md), [core/der.bastio](core-der.md), [core/p256.bastio](core-p256.md), [core/sha512.bastio](core-sha512.md), [core/rsa.bastio](core-rsa.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`tls13_client_hello`](#tls13_client_hello) | The ClientHello message (handshake type 1) offering TLS 1.3 with TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, the group X25519 (with the key share `key_share`, 32 bytes) and the signature schemes ed25519, ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256, ecdsa_secp384r1_sha384, rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 and rsa_pss_rsae_sha384, for the server named `server_name` (the host name, at most 255 bytes; empty for none). |
| [`tls13_client_hello_alpn`](#tls13_client_hello_alpn) | `tls13_client_hello` that also offers the application protocols `alpn` (RFC 7301). |
| [`tls13_client_hello_v12`](#tls13_client_hello_v12) | A ClientHello that offers TLS 1.3 as `tls13_client_hello_alpn` does and TLS 1.2 too. |
| [`tls13_parse_server_hello`](#tls13_parse_server_hello) | The X25519 public key (32 bytes) in the ServerHello `msg` (the whole handshake message, with its 4-byte header), or `None` unless it is a ServerHello for what `tls13_client_hello` offers. |
| [`tls13_server_hello_suite`](#tls13_server_hello_suite) | The cipher suite a ServerHello `msg` chose. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `tls13_client_hello`

```bastio
fn tls13_client_hello(random: &Bytes, session_id: &Bytes, server_name: &Bytes, key_share: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(random) == 32 && blen(session_id) == 32 && blen(key_share) == 32 && blen(server_name) <= 255
  ensures blen(result) > 4 && blen(result) < 600
```

The ClientHello message (handshake type 1) offering TLS 1.3 with
TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, the group X25519 (with the key share
`key_share`, 32 bytes) and the signature schemes ed25519,
ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256, ecdsa_secp384r1_sha384, rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 and
rsa_pss_rsae_sha384, for the server named
`server_name` (the host name, at most 255 bytes; empty for none). `random` and
`session_id` are 32 bytes each; the session id is echoed back by the
server and exists for compatibility with middleboxes. The result starts
with the type and a 3-byte length of what follows.

Example:

```bastio
let random = balloc(32);
let sid = balloc(32);
let key = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let hello = tls13_client_hello(random, sid, name, key);
let n = blen(hello);
let ty = bget(hello, 0);
let ln = load_be16(hello, 2);
bfree(hello);
bfree(name);
bfree(key);
bfree(sid);
bfree(random);
if ty != 1 || cast[u64](ln) + 4 != n { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_client_hello_alpn`

```bastio
fn tls13_client_hello_alpn(random: &Bytes, session_id: &Bytes, server_name: &Bytes, key_share: &Bytes, alpn: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(random) == 32 && blen(session_id) == 32 && blen(key_share) == 32 && blen(server_name) <= 255 && blen(alpn) <= 256
  ensures blen(result) > 4 && blen(result) < 900
```

`tls13_client_hello` that also offers the application protocols `alpn`
(RFC 7301): the ProtocolNameList without its own length, each name behind
a one-byte length (for example the bytes 8 and "http/1.1"), at most 256
bytes; empty offers none and gives what `tls13_client_hello` gives.

Example:

```bastio
let random = balloc(32);
let sid = balloc(32);
let key = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let mut a = text_new();
text_push(&mut a, 8);
text_push_str(&mut a, "http/1.1");
let alpn = text_finish(a);
let plain = tls13_client_hello(random, sid, name, key);
let hello = tls13_client_hello_alpn(random, sid, name, key, alpn);
let n = blen(hello);
let ln = load_be16(hello, 2);
let grew = n == blen(plain) + 4 + 2 + blen(alpn);
bfree(hello);
bfree(plain);
bfree(alpn);
bfree(name);
bfree(key);
bfree(sid);
bfree(random);
if cast[u64](ln) + 4 != n || !grew { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_client_hello_v12`

```bastio
fn tls13_client_hello_v12(random: &Bytes, session_id: &Bytes, server_name: &Bytes, key_share: &Bytes, alpn: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(random) == 32 && blen(session_id) == 32 && blen(key_share) == 32 && blen(server_name) <= 255 && blen(alpn) <= 256
  ensures blen(result) > 4 && blen(result) < 1200
```

A ClientHello that offers TLS 1.3 as `tls13_client_hello_alpn` does and
TLS 1.2 too: supported_versions lists both, the TLS 1.2 suites
ECDHE_{ECDSA,RSA}_WITH_{AES_128_GCM_SHA256, AES_256_GCM_SHA384,
CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256} follow the TLS 1.3 ones, the signature schemes
add rsa_pkcs1_sha256/384/512, and it asks for the extended master secret
(RFC 7627) and secure renegotiation (an empty renegotiation_info, RFC
5746) with uncompressed points. The key exchange is X25519 only;
secp256r1 and secp384r1 are listed for the curves of ECDSA certificates.

Example:

```bastio
let random = balloc(32);
let sid = balloc(32);
let key = balloc(32);
let name = bfrom("example.com");
let alpn = balloc(0);
let hello = tls13_client_hello_v12(random, sid, name, key, alpn);
let n = blen(hello);
let ln = load_be16(hello, 2);
bfree(hello);
bfree(alpn);
bfree(name);
bfree(key);
bfree(sid);
bfree(random);
if cast[u64](ln) + 4 != n { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_parse_server_hello`

```bastio
fn tls13_parse_server_hello(msg: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(msg) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 32
```

The X25519 public key (32 bytes) in the ServerHello `msg` (the whole
handshake message, with its 4-byte header), or `None` unless it is a
ServerHello for what `tls13_client_hello` offers: TLS 1.2 in the legacy
version, the suite TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, no compression, exactly
the extensions supported_versions (TLS 1.3) and key_share (x25519, once
each), and the length of each part inside the one before it. A
HelloRetryRequest is refused.

Example:

```bastio
let random = balloc(32);
let sid = balloc(32);
let key = balloc(32);
let name = balloc(0);
let hello = tls13_client_hello(random, sid, name, key);
let mut ok = false;
match tls13_parse_server_hello(hello) {
  Option::Some(k) => { bfree(k); },
  Option::None => { ok = true; },
}
bfree(hello);
bfree(name);
bfree(key);
bfree(sid);
bfree(random);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_server_hello_suite`

```bastio
fn tls13_server_hello_suite(msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires blen(msg) < 274877906944
  ensures result == 0 || result == 4865 || result == 4866 || result == 4867
```

The cipher suite a ServerHello `msg` chose: 4865 (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,
0x1301), 4866 (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, 0x1302) or 4867
(TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, 0x1303), or 0 when the
message is too short to hold one or names another.

Example:

```bastio
let msg = balloc(60);
let s = tls13_server_hello_suite(msg);
bfree(msg);
if s != 0 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `tls13_push_u16`

```bastio
fn tls13_push_u16(t: &mut Vec[u8], v: u64)
  requires v < 65536
  ensures vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + 2
```

Internal: appends the 16-bit big-endian number `v` to `t`.

### `tls13_push_block16`

```bastio
fn tls13_push_block16(t: &mut Vec[u8], b: &Bytes)
  requires blen(b) < 65536
  ensures vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + 2 + blen(b)
```

Internal: appends `b` to `t`, behind its length as a 16-bit number.

### `tls13_push_ext`

```bastio
fn tls13_push_ext(t: &mut Vec[u8], ty: u64, body: &Bytes)
  requires ty < 65536 && blen(body) < 65536
  ensures vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + 4 + blen(body)
```

Internal: appends the extension of type `ty` with the contents `body`.

### `tls13_u16_list`

```bastio
fn tls13_u16_list(a: u64, b: u64, c: u64, d: u64, e: u64, n: u64) -> Bytes
  requires a < 65536 && b < 65536 && c < 65536 && d < 65536 && e < 65536 && n >= 1 && n <= 5
  ensures blen(result) == 2 + 2 * n
```

Internal: the contents of a list of 16-bit numbers `a`, `b`, ... (the
first `n` of five) behind their length.

### `tls13_hello_extensions`

```bastio
fn tls13_hello_extensions(server_name: &Bytes, key_share: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(key_share) == 32 && blen(server_name) <= 255
  ensures blen(result) <= 340
```

Internal: the extensions of a ClientHello, behind none of their length.

### `tls13_hrr_random`

```bastio
fn tls13_hrr_random() -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

Internal: the random value that marks a HelloRetryRequest.

### `tls13_nib`

```bastio
fn tls13_nib(c: u8) -> u8
  ensures result < 16
```

Internal: the value of the hex digit `c`.

### `tls13_push_u24`

```bastio
fn tls13_push_u24(t: &mut Vec[u8], v: u64)
  requires v < 16777216
  ensures vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + 3
```

Internal: appends the 24-bit big-endian number `v` to `t`.

### `tls13_wrap`

```bastio
fn tls13_wrap(ty: u8, body: Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(body) < 16777216
  ensures blen(result) == blen(body) + 4
```

Internal: the handshake message of type `ty` with the contents `body`.

### `tls13_der_len`

```bastio
fn tls13_der_len(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u64
  requires at <= blen(b)
  ensures result == 0 || (result >= 2 && result <= blen(b) - at)
```

Internal: the length of the DER element at `b[at..]` with its header, or
0 when it is not a SEQUENCE that fits.

### `tls13_certificate_msg`

```bastio
fn tls13_certificate_msg(chain: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(chain) < 1048576
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) < 8388608
```

Internal: the Certificate message for the DER certificates `chain`, or
None when they do not split into certificates.

### `tls13_der_int`

```bastio
fn tls13_der_int(t: &mut Vec[u8], b: &Bytes, from: u64)
  requires from + 32 <= blen(b)
  ensures vlen(t) <= vlen(old(t)) + 35
```

Internal: appends the DER INTEGER for the 32-byte big-endian number at
`b[from..from+32]`.

### `tls13_sign`

```bastio
fn tls13_sign(kind: u64, ka: &Bytes, kb: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, content: &Bytes, scheme: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(ka) < 65536 && blen(kb) < 65536 && blen(nonce) < 1024 && (blen(content) == 130 || blen(content) == 146)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) <= 512
```

Internal: the signature over `content` (the CertificateVerify contents) of
the key `kind` (1 RSA: `ka` the modulus, `kb` the private exponent; 2 ECDSA
P-256: `ka` the scalar) under `scheme` (1027 or 2052), or None. `nonce` is
32 secret bytes that are not used again.

### `tls13_client_signed_content`

```bastio
fn tls13_client_signed_content(h: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(h) == 32 || blen(h) == 48
  ensures blen(result) == 98 + blen(h)
```

Internal: what the client signs in its CertificateVerify.
